senses.collocation_zh: 定冠词；定指名词短语
senses.sentence_en: English uses the definite article in the phrase 'the moon'.
senses.sentence_zh: 英语在短语 the moon 中使用定冠词。

etymology_story.zh: definite 来自拉丁语 definitus，即 definire（划定界限、界定）的过去分词；其中 finis 表示“边界、终点”。“界限已经划清”的概念发展为现代英语中的“明确的、确定的”，并与 define 保持词源联系。
etymology_story.en: Definite comes from Latin definitus, the past participle of definire (“to set boundaries or define”), which contains finis (“boundary or end”). The idea of having boundaries clearly established developed into “clear” and “certain,” and connects the word historically with define.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 definite 宜作为完整形容词词基掌握，不宜机械拆成 define + -ite。直接派生：definite + -ly → definitely（肯定地）、definite + -ness → definiteness（明确性）、in- + definite → indefinite（不确定的），以及 indefinitely（无限期地、不明确地）、indefiniteness（不确定性）；相关词族还有 define（界定）、definition（定义）、definable（可界定的）、definability（可界定性）、definitional（定义的）、redefine（重新界定）、redefinition（重新界定）、undefined（未定义的）、definitive（权威性的、最终的）、definitively（决定性地、最终地）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, definite is best treated as a whole adjective base, rather than mechanically split into define + -ite. Direct derivatives include definite + -ly → definitely, definite + -ness → definiteness, in- + definite → indefinite, plus indefinitely and indefiniteness. Related family members include define, definition, definable, definability, definitional, redefine, redefinition, undefined, definitive, and definitively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: clear（清楚的）强调容易理解或辨认；certain（确定的、确信的）强调没有疑问；specific（具体的）强调指向明确的细节或对象。definite 常强调内容已经明确或事情已经确定。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Clear emphasizes ease of understanding or recognition; certain emphasizes the absence of doubt; specific emphasizes particular details or a particular referent. Definite often emphasizes that something has been clearly established or settled.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把“边界划清”作为锚点：范围清楚，答案就 definite；definitely 表示“肯定地”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a clearly drawn boundary: once the limits are settled, something is definite; definitely means “certainly.”

senses.meaning_zh: 自由地；不受限制地
senses.meaning_en: Without restriction, obstruction, or outside control.

senses.meaning_en: In large amounts or without holding back.

etymology_story.zh: freely 延续了古英语中由 free 的早期形式和副词后缀构成的词，现代形式清楚体现 free + -ly。“不受束缚”的核心意义扩展为自愿、坦率、慷慨或不收费等用法。
etymology_story.en: Freely continues an Old English adverb formed from an earlier form of free and an adverbial suffix; its modern form transparently shows free + -ly. The central idea of being unrestricted extends to willing, open, generous, and cost-free action or access.

morphology_enriched.zh: free（自由的）+ -ly（以某种方式）→ freely（自由地）。主要词族：free（自由的；免费的；释放）、freer／freest（比较级／最高级）、frees／freed／freeing（动词变化形式）、freely（自由地）、freedom（自由）、freeness（自由或无约束的状态，较少见）、unfree（不自由的）；常见复合形式有 carefree（无忧无虑的）、freelance（自由职业的；从事自由职业）和 free-flowing（流动顺畅的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Free + -ly, an adverb-forming suffix, → freely. Main family members are free as an adjective and verb; freer/freest; frees/freed/freeing; freely; freedom; the less common freeness; and unfree. Common compounds include carefree, freelance, and free-flowing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: openly（公开地、坦率地）强调不隐瞒；willingly（自愿地、乐意地）强调主观愿意；generously（慷慨地）强调给予充足。freely 可分别表达这些意思，也可单纯表示没有限制。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Openly emphasizes a lack of concealment; willingly emphasizes readiness and personal choice; generously emphasizes giving abundantly. Freely can express each of these ideas and can also simply mean “without restriction.”

mnemonic_anchor.zh: free + -ly＝行动没有束缚：活动自由、表达坦率、给予大方。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Free + -ly means acting without restraint: move without barriers, speak without concealment, and give without holding back.

senses.meaning_zh: 善良；美德；善意

etymology_story.zh: goodness 经中古英语延续自古英语 godnes，由 good 的早期形式加表示性质或状态的名词后缀构成，核心意义是“好的品质”。其感叹用法后来成为提及 God 时较温和的替代表达。
etymology_story.en: Goodness came through Middle English from Old English godnes, formed from an earlier form of good and a noun-forming suffix meaning a quality or state. Its use as an exclamation later developed as a mild substitute for invoking God.

morphology_enriched.zh: good（好的、善良的）+ -ness（性质或状态）→ goodness（善良；有益品质）。核心词族：good、goodness；better 和 best 是 good 的不规则比较级和最高级。相关常用复合词有 goodwill（善意、友好）、good-hearted（心地善良的）、good-natured（脾气好的）和 good-looking（好看的）；goods 表示“商品”，不等于 goodness。
morphology_enriched.en: Good + -ness (“quality or state”) → goodness. The core family contains good and goodness; better and best are the irregular comparative and superlative forms of good. Related common compounds include goodwill, good-hearted, good-natured, and good-looking. Goods means merchandise and is distinct from goodness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: kindness（善良、体贴）强调关心和善待他人的行为；virtue（美德）强调符合道德标准的品质；benevolence（仁慈、善意）较正式，强调希望并促进他人幸福的意愿。goodness 是涵盖善良与道德品质的宽泛词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Kindness emphasizes considerate treatment of others; virtue emphasizes a morally admirable quality; benevolence is more formal and emphasizes wishing and promoting others' welfare. Goodness is the broader term for moral worth and kindness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: good + -ness＝“好的品质”：在人是善良，在食物是营养；My goodness! 单独记作“天哪！”
mnemonic_anchor.en: Good + -ness names a good quality: kindness in people and nourishment in food. Remember 'My goodness!' separately as a mild exclamation.

etymology_story.zh: historically 由 historical 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。其词族最终可追溯至希腊语 historia，意为“探究、通过探究获得的知识或记述”，后来发展出对过去事件的记述这一含义。
etymology_story.en: Historically was formed from historical with the adverb-forming suffix -ly. Its word family ultimately goes back to Greek historia, meaning inquiry, knowledge gained through inquiry, or an account, which developed into the idea of an account of past events.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：historical + -ly → historically；进一步可分析为 historic + -al → historical，其中 history 在派生时采用 histor- 这一词干形式。主要词族：history（历史）、historic（具有重大历史意义的）、historical（与历史有关的）、historically（历史上）、historian（历史学家）、historicity（历史真实性）、prehistory（史前史）、prehistoric（史前的）、ahistorical（忽视历史背景的）、unhistorical（不符合史实的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: historical + -ly → historically; historical can further be analyzed as historic + -al, with history using the stem form histor- in derivation. The principal family includes history, historic (important in history), historical (related to history), historically, historian (a person who studies history), historicity (historical actuality), prehistory, prehistoric, ahistorical (disregarding historical context), and unhistorical (inconsistent with historical facts).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: traditionally（传统上）强调沿袭的习俗或做法；formerly（以前）强调过去如此，且通常暗示现在已有变化；in the past（过去）只是一般时间说明。historically 更突出历史记录、长期趋势或历史背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Traditionally emphasizes inherited customs or practices; formerly describes an earlier situation and usually suggests that it has changed; in the past is a general time expression. Historically places greater emphasis on historical records, long-term patterns, or historical context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: historical（历史的）加 -ly：把事情放进历史时间线里看。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical + -ly: view something against the timeline of history.

etymology_story.zh: importantly 由 important 加 -ly 构成。important 经法语传入英语，最终与拉丁语 importare 有关；该词原有“带入”的意思，后来产生“具有意义、关系重大”的含义。
etymology_story.en: Importantly was formed by adding -ly to important. Important entered English through French and ultimately belongs to the family of Latin importare, originally meaning to bring in and later developing the sense of signifying or being consequential.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：important + -ly → importantly；important 在现代英语中通常作为完整词基使用，不宜把它简单理解成名词 import 加 -ant。主要词族：important（重要的）、importance（重要性）、importantly（重要的是；自命不凡地）、unimportant（不重要的）、unimportance（无足轻重）、self-important（自命不凡的）、self-importance（自命不凡）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: important + -ly → importantly; important normally functions as a whole base in modern English rather than as the noun import plus -ant. The principal family includes important, importance, importantly, unimportant, unimportance (lack of importance), self-important (having an exaggerated sense of one's importance), and self-importance.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: crucially（至关重要的是）强调对结果具有决定性作用；significantly（值得注意的是）强调某事有意义或能说明问题；pompously（自负地、浮夸地）对应 importantly 的行为方式义，并更突出言行的夸张做作。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Crucially emphasizes something decisive for the outcome; significantly highlights something meaningful or revealing; pompously overlaps with the manner sense of importantly but places greater emphasis on inflated, pretentious behavior.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: important 加 -ly：用于事实，就是“这点很重要”；用于人的举止，就是“他觉得自己很重要”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Important + -ly: applied to a fact, it means this matters; applied to someone's manner, it suggests they think they matter.

senses.meaning_zh: 在当地；在本地区

etymology_story.zh: locally 由 local 加 -ly 构成；local 经法语和拉丁语 localis，最终源于拉丁语 locus，意为“地方”。“与某个地方有关”的概念后来也用于身体局部、有限范围和计算机本机环境。
etymology_story.en: Locally was formed from local plus -ly; local came through French and Latin localis, ultimately from Latin locus, meaning place. The idea of a particular place also came to cover parts of the body, limited areas, and a computer's own environment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：local + -ly → locally；local 是直接词基，历史上的 loc- 表示“地方”。主要词族：local（当地的；当地人）、locally（在当地；在局部）、locality（地区、地点）、localize/localise（使局限于某处；使本地化）、localized/localised（局部的；本地化的）、localization/localisation（局部化；本地化）、localism（地方特色；地方主义）、nonlocal（非局部的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: local + -ly → locally; local is the immediate base, while historical loc- means place. The principal family includes local (an adjective or a noun meaning a local resident), locally, locality (an area or place), localize/localise (restrict to a place or adapt for local use), localized/localised, localization/localisation, localism (a local feature or an emphasis on local interests), and nonlocal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nearby（在附近）强调距离近，不一定属于同一行政或社会区域；regionally（在地区范围内）通常涉及比 local 更大的地域；on-site（在现场）强调在某个指定地点。locally 的核心是限定在当前所指的地方、局部或设备。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nearby emphasizes physical closeness without requiring the same administrative or social area; regionally usually covers a larger geographical area; on-site emphasizes a specified physical location. Locally refers to the particular area, part, or device relevant to the context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: local 的核心是“这个地方”：城镇里是当地，整体里是局部，电脑上是本机。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Local means this particular place: the local area, one part of a whole, or your own computer.

etymology_story.zh: machinery 与 machine 加集合名词后缀 -ery 的构词方式及法语 machinerie 有关；machine 最终源于希腊语 mēkhanē，意为“器具、装置或手段”。该词从机械设备的集合，扩展为像机器一样协调运作的组织或制度。
etymology_story.en: Machinery is associated with machine plus the collective noun suffix -ery and with French machinerie; machine ultimately comes from Greek mēkhanē, meaning a device, contrivance, or means. The word expanded from mechanical equipment to organizations and systems whose parts work together like a machine.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：machine 去掉词尾不发音的 e，再加 -ery → machinery，表示相关设备的集合或系统。主要词族：machine（机器；用机器加工）、machinery（机器设备；运作机制）、machinist（机械加工工人）、machining（机械加工）、machinable（可机械加工的）；同源相关词包括 mechanism（机制）、mechanic（机械师）、mechanical（机械的）、mechanically（机械地）、mechanize/mechanise（使机械化）、mechanization/mechanisation（机械化）。machinery 不可数，单件设备可说 a machine 或 a piece of machinery。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: machine drops its final silent e and takes -ery → machinery, denoting a collection or system of equipment. The principal family includes machine (noun and verb), machinery, machinist (a worker who operates machine tools), machining (shaping material with machine tools), and machinable. Related words of shared origin include mechanism, mechanic, mechanical, mechanically, mechanize/mechanise, and mechanization/mechanisation. Machinery is uncountable; an individual item is a machine or a piece of machinery.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: equipment（设备）范围最广，也包括非机械工具；machines（机器）是可数复数，突出一台台具体机器；apparatus（装置；机构）常指为特定目的组织起来的一套器具或体系。machinery 强调机械设备的整体，或复杂体系的协同运作。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Equipment is broader and includes nonmechanical tools; machines is a countable plural that highlights individual machines; apparatus often denotes a set of devices or an organizational system serving a particular purpose. Machinery emphasizes mechanical equipment collectively or the coordinated operation of a complex system.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: machine 加集合后缀 -ery：一整套机器；机构也像一整套机器那样运转。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Machine + collective -ery: a whole set of machines; an institution can operate like one too.

senses.meaning_zh: 即；也就是；具体说来
senses.meaning_en: used to specify exactly who or what has just been referred to
senses.english_definition: You use namely to introduce the exact person, thing, or details that you have just referred to more generally.
senses.collocation_en: one main reason, namely; two factors, namely
senses.collocation_zh: 一个主要原因，即；两个因素，即

etymology_story.zh: namely 承自中古英语 nameliche，与 name 和副词后缀有关，早期曾有“特别地、尤其”等用法。其现代含义逐渐固定为明确说出前文所指的具体名称或内容。
etymology_story.en: Namely descends from Middle English nameliche, a formation related to name and an adverbial suffix, with earlier uses such as particularly or especially. Its modern meaning settled on explicitly identifying the person, thing, or details previously referred to.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代形式可分析为 name + -ly → namely，但它已是词义固定的说明性副词，不能机械理解为“以名字的方式”。主要词族：name（名字；命名）、named（被命名的）、naming（命名）、nameless（无名的）、namelessness（无名状态）、namesake（同名者）、rename（重新命名）、misname（叫错名字）、unnamed（未具名的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern form can be analyzed as name + -ly → namely, but it is a lexicalized specifying adverb rather than simply meaning in a name-like manner. The principal family includes name (noun and verb), named, naming, nameless, namelessness (the state of having no name), namesake (a person or thing sharing another's name), rename, misname, and unnamed.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: that is（也就是说）可用于释义、改述或纠正；specifically（具体来说）可缩小范围或突出某一点；in particular（尤其）通常从较大集合中选出重点。namely 则明确列出或点明前文所指的内容，通常引出完整说明，而非随意举例。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: That is can explain, rephrase, or correct; specifically can narrow the scope or highlight a detail; in particular usually singles out an item from a larger set. Namely explicitly identifies what the preceding expression refers to, normally introducing a full specification rather than an illustrative example.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 看到 name，就想到“把名字点出来”：先概括，再用 namely 明确指出具体是谁或是什么。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of name: first give the general description, then use namely to name exactly who or what you mean.

translation: 讲座考察了民族主义如何塑造该运动面向公众的信息。
usage_note: nationalism 涉及把国家或民族身份置于政治、文化或社会讨论中心；具体立场必须由上下文说明。

senses.meaning_zh: 民族主义；强调本民族或国家利益、认同与团结的思想，有时包含优越意识
senses.meaning_en: Strong identification with a nation and support for its interests, sometimes involving a belief in its superiority.
senses.english_definition: Nationalism is a strong feeling of loyalty to your nation and a belief that its interests are especially important, sometimes more important than those of other nations.
senses.collocation_en: a rise in nationalism; economic nationalism
senses.collocation_zh: 民族主义的兴起；经济民族主义
senses.sentence_en: The campaign appealed to economic nationalism by promising to protect domestic industries.
senses.sentence_zh: 这场竞选活动承诺保护本国产业，以此迎合经济民族主义情绪。

senses.meaning_zh: 争取民族独立或自治的思想与运动
senses.meaning_en: The belief or movement that a nation should govern itself.
senses.english_definition: Nationalism is the desire of a people who share a national identity to have their own independent country or to govern themselves.
senses.collocation_en: anti-colonial nationalism; the growth of nationalism
senses.collocation_zh: 反殖民民族主义；民族主义的发展
senses.sentence_en: Anti-colonial nationalism helped unite people demanding independence.
senses.sentence_zh: 反殖民民族主义帮助要求独立的人们团结起来。

etymology_story.zh: nationalism 形成于 national（民族的；国家的）与 -ism（思想体系；运动）的构词关系中，其历史发展也与法语 nationalisme 密切相关。它逐渐用于指称强调民族认同、国家利益或民族自主的思想与运动。
etymology_story.en: Nationalism belongs to the formation national + -ism, and its historical development is closely associated with French nationalisme. It came to describe ideas and movements emphasizing national identity, national interests, or national self-government.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：national + -ism → nationalism；national 又由 nation + -al 构成。常用词族包括 nation（民族；国家）、national（国家的；国民）、nationally（在全国范围内）、nationality（国籍；民族身份）、nationalism（民族主义）、nationalist（民族主义者；民族主义的）、nationalistic（民族主义的，常含过强倾向）、nationalistically（以民族主义方式）、nationhood（民族或国家的独立存在状态）。扩展词族包括 nationalize/nationalise（使国有化）、nationalization/nationalisation（国有化）、international（国际的）、internationalism（国际主义）、internationalist（国际主义者）、multinational（跨国的）及 nationwide（全国性的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: national + -ism → nationalism; national itself is nation + -al. Common family members include nation, national, nationally, nationality, nationalism, nationalist, nationalistic, nationalistically, and nationhood. The extended family includes nationalize/nationalise and nationalization/nationalisation, referring to state ownership; international, internationalism, and internationalist; multinational; and nationwide.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: patriotism（爱国主义）侧重对国家的热爱与奉献；national consciousness（民族意识）侧重共同身份的觉醒，并不必然包含政治主张；separatism（分离主义）侧重脱离现有国家的诉求，仅与部分民族主义运动重合。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Patriotism emphasizes love of and commitment to one's country; national consciousness emphasizes awareness of a shared identity without necessarily implying a political program; separatism emphasizes breaking away from an existing state and overlaps with only some nationalist movements.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: nation 是“民族或国家”，-ism 是“一套主张”：把民族或国家放在政治关注的中心。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Nation names the community; -ism names a system of ideas: nationalism puts the nation at the center of political concern.

senses.pos: adj. 形容词（尤用于英式英语）

senses.meaning_en: Served without water, ice, or another drink.
senses.english_definition: A neat alcoholic drink, especially a spirit, has no water, ice, or other drink added to it.
senses.collocation_en: neat whisky; drink it neat
senses.collocation_zh: 不加水或冰的威士忌；直接纯饮

etymology_story.zh: neat 经中古英语和法语 net 追溯到拉丁语 nitidus，原意涉及“明亮、洁净、讲究”。它后来发展出“整洁、利落、巧妙”等意义；用于酒时表示未掺入其他东西。
etymology_story.en: Neat came through Middle English and French net from Latin nitidus, associated with brightness, cleanliness, and elegance. It developed meanings such as tidy, skillful, and clever, while its use for drinks describes an unmixed spirit.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 neat 是不可再按常用词缀拆分的基本形容词，不宜分析为 n- + eat。屈折形式为 neater（更整洁的；更巧妙的）和 neatest（最整洁的；最巧妙的）；派生词为 neatly（整齐地；巧妙地）和 neatness（整洁；利落）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, neat is a base adjective with no productive internal affix boundary; it should not be divided into n- + eat. Its comparative and superlative forms are neater and neatest, and its derivatives are neatly and neatness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tidy（整齐的）强调物品摆放有序；clever（巧妙的）强调方法或想法体现智慧，与 neat 的“简洁巧妙”义接近；undiluted（未稀释的）强调浓度未被降低，而酒类中的 neat 还通常排除加冰和其他饮料。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tidy emphasizes orderly arrangement; clever emphasizes intelligence in an idea or method and overlaps with neat meaning elegantly effective; undiluted emphasizes unchanged concentration, whereas neat for spirits normally also excludes ice and mixers.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“干净利落”的感觉：房间整齐，办法巧妙，酒里不掺别的；口语中还可赞“真棒”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think clean and well finished: an orderly room, an elegant solution, or an unmixed drink; informally, something neat can simply be great.

senses.meaning_en: Making or filled with a lot of noise.
senses.english_definition: Someone or something that is noisy makes a lot of noise, and a noisy place has a lot of noise in it.
senses.collocation_en: a noisy crowd; a noisy street
senses.collocation_zh: 吵闹的人群；嘈杂的街道

senses.meaning_zh: （信号、数据或图像）含噪声的；受随机干扰的
senses.meaning_en: Containing unwanted interference or random variation.
senses.english_definition: Noisy data, signals, or images contain unwanted variation or interference that makes useful information harder to identify.
senses.collocation_en: noisy data; a noisy signal
senses.collocation_zh: 含噪声的数据；受噪声干扰的信号
senses.sentence_en: The researchers collected more samples because the initial data were noisy.
senses.sentence_zh: 由于最初的数据中随机干扰较多，研究人员又采集了更多样本。

etymology_story.zh: noisy 由 noise 加形容词后缀 -y 构成；noise 经中古英语来自古法语，早期意义涉及喧闹、纷扰和争吵。现代技术语境又把“噪声”扩展为信号或数据中妨碍识别信息的干扰。
etymology_story.en: Noisy was formed from noise with the adjective suffix -y; noise entered Middle English from Old French, with early meanings involving disturbance, uproar, and quarrelling. In modern technical use, noise also means interference that obscures information in signals or data.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：noise 去掉词尾不发音的 e，再加 -y → noisy，表示“具有噪声特征的”。屈折形式为 noisier、noisiest；派生词为 noisily（吵闹地）和 noisiness（嘈杂程度）。同族词包括 noise（噪声；喧闹声）、noiseless（无声的）、noiselessly（无声地）和 noiselessness（无声状态）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: noise drops its final silent e before taking -y → noisy, meaning characterized by noise. Its comparative and superlative are noisier and noisiest; derivatives are noisily and noisiness. Related forms include noise, noiseless, noiselessly, and noiselessness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: loud（声音大的）强调音量，不一定令人不快；rowdy（吵闹失控的）多描述人群或行为，包含不守秩序的意味；clamorous（喧嚷的）强调持续或强烈的吵闹、叫喊。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Loud emphasizes volume without necessarily implying annoyance; rowdy usually describes people or behavior and suggests disorder; clamorous emphasizes insistent or intense noise, especially shouting.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: noise + -y＝“噪声多的”：耳朵听着吵，数据看着乱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Noise + -y means full of noise: it can overwhelm your ears or obscure a pattern in data.

senses.pos: adj. 形容词（通常用于名词前）
senses.meaning_zh: 外部的；外层的；远离中心的
senses.meaning_en: On the outside or farther from the center.
senses.english_definition: The outer part of something is on its outside or farther from its center than other parts.
senses.collocation_en: the outer layer; outer space
senses.collocation_zh: 外层；外太空
senses.sentence_en: The outer layer protects the fruit from damage.

senses.pos: adj. 形容词（通常用于名词前）
senses.meaning_zh: 外在的；表面的；显露于外的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to outward appearance rather than inner feelings or qualities.
senses.english_definition: Someone's outer appearance or behavior is what other people can see, as opposed to their private feelings or inner qualities.
senses.collocation_en: outer appearance; outer calm
senses.collocation_zh: 外在形象；表面的平静
senses.sentence_en: Her outer calm concealed how worried she really was.
senses.sentence_zh: 她表面的平静掩盖了内心深深的担忧。

etymology_story.zh: outer 源于古英语表示“更靠外”的比较形式，与 out 属于同一词源系统。这个历史比较义后来固定为表示“外部的、远离中心的”的形容词，并可引申为人的外在表现。
etymology_story.en: Outer descends from an Old English comparative form meaning farther out and belongs to the same historical family as out. That comparative meaning became an established adjective for exterior position and later also for outward appearance.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 outer 应作为独立形容词学习；历史上可联系 out 与比较形式，但不能据此把它当作普通形容词的规则比较级。直接相关形式有 outermost（最外面的）和 outerwear（外穿衣物）；同源及相关词包括 out（在外；向外）、outward/outwards（向外；outward 也可作形容词，表示外在的）和 outside（外面；外部的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, outer is best learned as an established adjective; its historical relationship to out and comparative formation does not make it an ordinary regular comparative today. Directly related forms include outermost and outerwear. Historical and semantic relatives include out, outward/outwards, and outside; outward also functions as an adjective meaning external or visible.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: external（外部的）适用范围更广，也可指来自系统之外的因素；exterior（外部的）常指物体或建筑的外表面；outward（外在的；向外的）强调朝外的方向或可观察到的表现，而 outer 常强调层次和相对位置。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: External has a wider range and can describe influences coming from outside a system; exterior often concerns the outside surface of an object or building; outward emphasizes direction or visible expression, while outer commonly emphasizes layers and relative position.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 out“外面”联想 outer“靠外的一层”：离中心更远，或显露在外。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link out with outer: the layer farther out, or the part of a person that others can see.

etymology_story.zh: painful 在中古英语中由 pain 与 -ful 构成；pain 经法语追溯到拉丁语 poena，意为“惩罚、刑罚”。这个词后来广泛用于身体疼痛、情绪痛苦，以及难堪或艰难的经历。
etymology_story.en: Painful was formed in Middle English from pain and -ful; pain came through French from Latin poena, meaning punishment or penalty. The adjective came to cover physical hurt, emotional suffering, and experiences that are awkward or difficult to endure.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：pain + -ful → painful，意为“具有痛苦性质的”或“引起痛苦的”；后缀 -ful 只写一个 l。比较形式为 more painful 和 most painful；派生词为 painfully（痛苦地；令人难受地；极其明显地）和 painfulness（疼痛；痛苦程度）。同族词包括 pain（疼痛；使痛苦）、pained（痛苦的；受伤的）、painless（无痛的）、painlessly（无痛地）、painlessness（无痛状态）、painkiller（止痛药）和 painkilling（止痛的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: pain + -ful → painful, meaning involving or causing pain; the suffix -ful has one l. Comparison uses more painful and most painful. Derivatives are painfully, which can also intensify an unpleasant quality, and painfulness. Related forms include pain, pained, painless, painlessly, painlessness, painkiller, and painkilling.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sore（疼痛的）常形容身体部位触碰或活动时的酸痛；distressing（令人苦恼的）主要强调情绪上的不安与痛苦；agonizing（令人极度痛苦的）程度更强，也可形容极难作出的决定。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sore commonly describes a body part that hurts when touched or moved; distressing primarily emphasizes emotional upset; agonizing is much stronger and can also describe an extremely difficult decision.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pain + -ful：带来“痛”的；身体会痛，回忆会痛，难堪和抉择也会让人难受。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pain + -ful: something that brings hurt—to the body, to your feelings, or through an awkward experience or difficult choice.

etymology_story.zh: pardon 在中古英语时期借自古法语 pardon（名词）和 pardoner（动词），最终可追溯到后期拉丁语 perdonare，意为“彻底给予；宽恕”。其意义由宽恕过错发展出正式赦免，以及请求原谅或重复话语的礼貌表达。
etymology_story.en: Middle English borrowed pardon from Old French pardon, a noun, and pardoner, a verb, ultimately from Late Latin perdonare, meaning to give completely or forgive. Forgiveness developed into the legal sense of an official pardon and polite expressions requesting forgiveness or repetition.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 pardon 通常作为完整词干学习，不宜强拆为现代英语前后缀；历史上的 per- 表示“彻底”，donare 表示“给予”。词族包括 pardon（原谅；赦免）、pardonable（可原谅的）、pardonably（可以理解地；情有可原地）、unpardonable（不可原谅的）、unpardonably（不可原谅地）和 pardoner（赦免者；历史上兜售赎罪券者）；屈折形式为 pardons、pardoned、pardoning。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, pardon is normally treated as a whole stem rather than split into productive English affixes; historically, per- meant completely and donare meant give. Its family includes pardon, pardonable, pardonably, unpardonable, unpardonably, and pardoner, meaning someone who grants pardons or, historically, sells indulgences; inflected forms are pardons, pardoned, and pardoning.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: forgive（原谅）侧重个人不再责怪或怨恨；excuse（谅解；宽免）侧重认为过失可以理解或免除责任；pardon（原谅；赦免）在日常用语中较正式，在法律语境中可指官方赦免。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Forgive emphasizes letting go of blame or resentment; excuse emphasizes treating a fault as understandable or releasing someone from responsibility; pardon is more formal in everyday use and can specifically mean official forgiveness of a crime.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史逻辑：“彻底给予”宽恕 → 原谅过错、赦免罪行；“Pardon?” 则是在请求对方包涵并再说一遍。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical hook: give forgiveness completely → forgive a fault or pardon a crime; 'Pardon?' asks the listener's indulgence and a repetition.

etymology_story.zh: parental 经法语与拉丁语 parentalis 相联系，后者意为“父母的”，来自 parens，其词干为 parent-，意为“父母；生育者”。现代英语也自然地将其理解为 parent 加 -al，并将它用于生物学中的亲本关系。
etymology_story.en: Parental came through French from Latin parentalis, meaning relating to parents, from parens, with the stem parent-, meaning a parent or one who brings forth. Modern English also readily analyzes it as parent plus -al, and uses it for parent organisms in biology.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：parent（父母之一；亲本）+ -al（……的）→ parental。词族包括 parent（父亲或母亲；作动词指养育）、parents（父母）、parenting（养育；育儿）、parenthood（为人父母的身份或阶段）、parentage（出身；亲子血统）、parental（父母的；亲本的）和 parentally（以父母的方式）；parent 的动词屈折形式包括 parented、parenting。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: parent + -al, meaning relating to, → parental. The family includes parent as a noun and verb, parents, parenting, parenthood, parentage, parental, and parentally; verbal inflections of parent include parented and parenting.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: maternal（母亲的）专指母亲一方；paternal（父亲的）专指父亲一方；familial（家庭的；家族的）涵盖更广的家庭或家族关系，而 parental 具体涉及父母或亲本。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Maternal refers specifically to the mother; paternal refers specifically to the father; familial concerns the wider family, whereas parental specifically concerns parents or parent organisms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: parent + -al：给 parent 加上“……的”，就是“父母的”；生物学中则是“亲本的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Parent + -al means relating to a parent: parental duties in a family, parental traits in biology.

etymology_story.zh: partial 经古法语进入中古英语，最终来自后期拉丁语 partialis，源于 pars、partis，意为“部分”。“只涉及一部分”发展出“只站在一方”的偏袒义，继而形成 partial to 所表达的偏爱义。
etymology_story.en: Partial entered Middle English through Old French, ultimately from Late Latin partialis, based on pars, partis, meaning part. The idea of involving only one part developed into favoring one side and then into the liking expressed by partial to.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习中可分析为 part（部分）+ -ial（构成形容词的后缀）→ partial；历史上来自拉丁语词干 part- 加 -alis。核心词族包括 partial（部分的；偏袒的）、partially（部分地）、partiality（偏袒；偏爱）、impartial（公正的，im- 表示“不”）、impartially（公正地）和 impartiality（公正）；同基词还包括 part（部分；分开）、partly（部分地）和 partitive（表示部分的）。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern learning, partial can be analyzed as part + the adjective-forming suffix -ial; historically, it reflects Latin part- + -alis. Its core family includes partial, partially, partiality, impartial with negative im-, impartially, and impartiality; related formations from part include part itself, partly, and partitive.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: incomplete（不完整的）强调缺少必要部分；biased（有偏见的；偏袒的）强调判断偏向一方；fond of（喜欢）表达喜爱。partial 可分别对应这些意义，但“喜欢”义通常必须用 partial to。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Incomplete emphasizes missing necessary parts; biased emphasizes an unfair tendency in judgment; fond of expresses liking. Partial overlaps with each in a different sense, but its liking sense normally requires partial to.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 part“一部分”：只占一部分 → 不完全；只站一方 → 偏袒；心偏向某物 → partial to，偏爱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think part: only part of the whole → incomplete; only one side → biased; a preference leaning toward something → partial to.

etymology_story.zh: partially 由英语形容词 partial 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；partial 最终可追溯到表示“部分”的拉丁语 pars、partis。其现代常用义是“只达到部分程度”，而非完全达到。
etymology_story.en: Partially was formed in English by adding the adverbial suffix -ly to partial, which ultimately goes back to Latin pars, partis, meaning part. Its usual modern meaning describes something that reaches only a limited degree rather than completeness.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：partial（部分的）+ -ly（构成副词）→ partially，保留 partial 末尾的 l，再加 -ly，形成双写的 ll。相关词族包括 part（部分）、partial（部分的；偏袒的）、partly（部分地）、partiality（偏袒；偏爱）、impartial（公正的）、impartially（公正地）和 impartiality（公正）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: partial + the adverbial suffix -ly → partially; the final l of partial remains before -ly, producing ll. Related family members include part, partial, partly, partiality, impartial, impartially, and impartiality.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: partly（部分地）与 partially 常可互换，解释多种原因时尤其常见；incompletely（不完全地）更突出未完成或有所缺失；to some extent（在一定程度上）侧重程度上的有限成立。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Partly is often interchangeable with partially and is especially natural when explaining multiple causes; incompletely stresses unfinished work or missing elements; to some extent emphasizes limited degree or validity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: partial 是“部分的”，加 -ly 变“部分地”：进度条只走了一部分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Partial means involving a part; -ly makes it partially: picture a progress bar that is only partly filled.

senses.meaning_zh: 像照片一样精确详尽的；记忆异常清晰的

etymology_story.zh: photographic 形成于十九世纪摄影术兴起时期，与 photograph 加形容词后缀 -ic 相联系；photo- 源于希腊语表示“光”的 phōs、phōtos，-graph- 与表示“书写、描画”的 graphein 同源。其字面逻辑是“用光记录”，后来又用来形容记忆或描写像照片一样清晰精确。
etymology_story.en: Photographic arose in the nineteenth-century development of photography and is related to photograph plus -ic; photo- comes from Greek phōs, phōtos, meaning light, and -graph- is related to graphein, meaning write or draw. The underlying idea is recording with light, later extended to memory or description resembling a photograph in clarity and accuracy.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：photograph（照片；拍照）+ -ic（……的）→ photographic；也可识别 photo-（光；照片）+ -graph-（记录）+ -ic。词族包括 photo（照片；非正式用语）、photograph（照片；拍照）、photography（摄影；摄影术）、photographer（摄影师）、photographic（摄影的）、photographically（以摄影方式；如照片般地）；photograph 的屈折形式为 photographs、photographed、photographing。重音随构词变化：PHOtograph → phoTOGraphy／phoTOGrapher → photoGRAPHic。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: photograph + -ic → photographic; its elements can also be recognized as photo-, meaning light or photograph, -graph-, meaning recording, and -ic. The family includes photo, photograph as a noun and verb, photography, photographer, photographic, and photographically; verbal inflections are photographs, photographed, and photographing. Stress shifts across the family: PHOtograph → phoTOGraphy/phoTOGrapher → photoGRAPHic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: visual（视觉的）涵盖一切与观看有关的内容，比 photographic 范围广；pictorial（图画的；以图片表现的）可以涉及绘画或照片；lifelike（逼真的）强调效果像真实事物，不要求使用摄影技术。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Visual covers anything relating to sight and is broader than photographic; pictorial concerns representation through pictures, including drawings and photographs; lifelike emphasizes resemblance to reality without requiring photography.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: photo- 是“光”，-graph- 是“记录”：用光记录成照片；photographic memory 就像脑中存着清晰照片。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Photo- means light and -graph- means recording: a photograph records with light; a photographic memory recalls details as if a clear picture were stored in the mind.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：plan（计划）+ -er（执行者或工具）→ planner；添加后缀时双写 n。常用词族：plan（计划；打算）、plans（复数或第三人称单数）、planned（计划好的）、planning（规划；计划工作）、planner（规划者；计划本）、unplanned（未计划的）、replan（重新规划）、preplan（预先规划）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: plan + -er, denoting a person or tool; the final n is doubled before the suffix. Common family members are plan, plans, planned, planning, planner, unplanned, replan, and preplan.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: An organizer coordinates people and practical arrangements; a scheduler assigns times to activities; a diary, especially in British English, can record appointments or personal experiences, while a planner emphasizes future arrangements.

etymology_story.zh: problematic 经由法语和拉丁语追溯至希腊语 problēmatikos，与 problēma（提出的问题或任务）有关。其历史核心是“有待讨论或解决的”，现代常表示会造成困难或值得质疑。
etymology_story.en: Problematic can be traced through French and Latin to Greek problēmatikos, related to problēma, a question or task put forward. Its historical connection with matters requiring discussion or solution underlies its modern meanings of difficult and questionable.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族分析：problem（问题）+ -atic（形容词后缀）→ problematic；这是便于理解的词族分析，历史上该词是借入的。常用词族：problem、problematic、problematically（有问题地）、unproblematic（没有问题的）、unproblematically（顺利地；不存在问题地）、problematize／problematise（使问题化；对原有看法提出质疑）、problematization／problematisation（问题化）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern family analysis: problem + the adjective-forming suffix -atic → problematic; this explains the relationship, although the word was historically borrowed. Family members include problem, problematic, problematically, unproblematic, unproblematically, problematize/problematise, and problematization/problematisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: difficult（困难的）强调处理时需要付出努力；troublesome（麻烦的）强调带来不便或反复困扰；questionable（值得怀疑的）强调真实性、合理性或可接受性存疑。problematic 可同时涉及实际困难与原则上的问题。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Difficult emphasizes the effort needed to deal with something; troublesome emphasizes inconvenience or recurring trouble; questionable emphasizes doubts about truth, soundness, or acceptability. Problematic can cover both practical difficulties and objections in principle.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 problem：problematic 就是“带着问题的”，可能难处理，也可能站不住脚。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep problem in view: something problematic brings a problem, either in practice or in its underlying reasoning.

senses.meaning_zh: 务实态度；对现实的清醒认识
senses.meaning_en: a practical acceptance of facts and limitations
senses.english_definition: Realism is the ability or willingness to recognize the facts of a situation and make decisions based on them.
senses.collocation_en: a sense of realism; political realism

senses.sentence_zh: 对于今年能取得什么成果，我们需要有清醒的现实认识。

senses.meaning_zh: 现实主义；逼真性；写实风格
senses.meaning_en: the faithful representation of life in art or literature
senses.english_definition: Realism is a style of art or writing that shows people and events as they are in ordinary life, or the quality of seeming true to life.
senses.collocation_en: social realism; photographic realism
senses.collocation_zh: 社会现实主义；照片般的逼真效果
senses.sentence_en: The film combines emotional depth with striking realism.
senses.sentence_zh: 这部电影兼具深厚的情感和鲜明的真实感。

senses.meaning_zh: 实在论；认为某些事物独立于人的思想而存在的哲学立场
senses.meaning_en: the philosophical view that certain things exist independently of thought
senses.english_definition: In philosophy, realism is the view that the things being discussed exist independently of what people think or believe about them.
senses.collocation_en: scientific realism; moral realism
senses.collocation_zh: 科学实在论；道德实在论
senses.sentence_en: Scientific realism treats the entities described by successful theories as real.
senses.sentence_zh: 科学实在论认为，成功理论所描述的实体是真实存在的。

etymology_story.zh: realism 属于 real 加 -ism 的词族，与法语 réalisme 也有历史联系；real 最终可追溯至拉丁语 res，意为“事物”。该词用于讨论何者真实存在，也用于艺术中的如实表现，并形成了日常语言中“正视现实”的含义。
etymology_story.en: Realism belongs to the real + -ism family and is historically connected with French réalisme; real ultimately goes back to Latin res, meaning 'thing'. The word is used for views about what exists, faithful artistic representation, and a practical acceptance of reality.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：real（真实的）+ -ism（思想、流派或实践方式）→ realism。常用词族：real（真实的）、really（真正地）、reality（现实）、realness（真实感）、realist（现实主义者；务实者）、realistic（现实的；逼真的）、realistically（现实地）、unreal（不真实的）、unreality（非现实性）、unrealistic（不切实际的）、unrealistically（不切实际地）；相关动词词族包括 realize／realise（意识到；实现）、realization／realisation（认识；实现）、realizable／realisable（可实现的）、unrealizable／unrealisable（无法实现的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: real + -ism, denoting a doctrine, movement, or practice. Common family members include real, really, reality, realness, realist, realistic, realistically, unreal, unreality, unrealistic, and unrealistically. The related verb family includes realize/realise, realization/realisation, realizable/realisable, and unrealizable/unrealisable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pragmatism（实用主义；务实态度）强调实际效果，realism 强调承认事实和限制；verisimilitude（逼真性）指作品看起来真实的程度；naturalism（自然主义）在文艺中常指更具体的创作传统，与 realism 有重叠，但不能在所有语境中互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pragmatism emphasizes practical results, while realism emphasizes acknowledging facts and limits. Verisimilitude is the appearance of truth in a work. Naturalism can name a more specific artistic or literary tradition that overlaps with realism but is not interchangeable with it in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: real + -ism：把“真实”作为立足点——做事务实，创作写实，哲学讨论实在。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Real + -ism: take reality as your starting point in decisions, artistic representation, or philosophy.

senses.meaning_zh: 现实的；务实的；切实可行的
senses.meaning_en: based on actual conditions and reasonable expectations
senses.english_definition: If someone is realistic, they understand what is possible; if a plan or expectation is realistic, it fits the actual situation.

senses.collocation_zh: 切合实际的期望；切实可行的目标

etymology_story.zh: realistic 由 realist 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，与 real 和 realism 同属一个词族。它既表示表现方式贴近真实生活，也表示判断、目标或计划符合现实条件。
etymology_story.en: Realistic was formed from realist with the adjective suffix -ic and belongs to the same family as real and realism. It describes both representations that resemble life and judgments, goals, or plans that fit actual conditions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：real（真实的）+ -ist（持某种立场的人）→ realist，再加 -ic → realistic；也可整体识别为 real + -istic。直接派生：realistic + -ally → realistically（现实地；逼真地），un- + realistic → unrealistic（不切实际的），unrealistic + -ally → unrealistically（不切实际地）。基础词族还包括 real、really（真正地）、reality（现实）、realness（真实感）、realism（现实主义）、realist（现实主义者；务实者）、unreal（不真实的）和 unreality（非现实性）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: real + -ist → realist, then realist + -ic → realistic; the ending can also be recognized as -istic. Direct derivatives are realistically, unrealistic, and unrealistically. The underlying family also includes real, really, reality, realness, realism, realist, unreal, and unreality.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: practical（实际的；实用的）强调有用或便于实施；feasible（可行的）强调在现有条件下能够完成；lifelike（栩栩如生的）强调外观或表现像真的一样。realistic 可描述清醒的判断，也可描述逼真的再现。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Practical emphasizes usefulness or ease of implementation; feasible emphasizes whether something can be done under existing conditions; lifelike emphasizes resemblance to a real person or thing. Realistic can describe either sound expectations or convincing representation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 real：想法贴近现实就是“务实”，画面贴近真实就是“逼真”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Stay close to real: realistic plans fit reality, and realistic pictures resemble reality.

etymology_story.zh: ruler 由 rule 加 -er 构成，两个常见义项分别联系 rule 的“统治”和“画直线”之义。rule 经由古法语追溯至拉丁语 regula，原指直木条或准绳，后来也表示规则、指导和管理。
etymology_story.en: Ruler combines rule with -er, with its two familiar meanings connected to governing and drawing straight lines. Rule came through Old French from Latin regula, a straight rod or standard, which also developed meanings involving rules, guidance, and control.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：rule（统治；画直线）去词尾不发音的 e，再加 -er → ruler；-er 在这里既可表示执行者，也可表示工具。常用词族：rule（规则；统治）、rules（复数或第三人称单数）、ruled（受统治的；印有横线的）、ruling（裁决；执政的）、ruler（统治者；尺子）、rulership（统治地位）、misrule（暴政；治理不善）、overrule（否决）、unruly（难以管束的）、unruliness（难以管束的状态）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: rule drops its silent final e before -er → ruler; -er can identify either a person or an instrument. Common family members include rule, rules, ruled, ruling, ruler, rulership, misrule, overrule, unruly, and unruliness.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sovereign（君主；最高统治者）强调最高统治权；leader（领导者）范围更广，不一定拥有国家统治权；straightedge（直边尺）强调画直线或检查平直，可能没有刻度，而 ruler 通常带有测量刻度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A sovereign holds supreme ruling authority; a leader is a broader term and need not govern a state. A straightedge is used to draw or check straight lines and may have no graduations, whereas a ruler usually has a measuring scale.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: rule 可以“治理”，也可以“画直线”：ruler 一边管国家，一边管线条。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Rule can mean govern or draw lines: a ruler governs a country or guides a straight line.

etymology_story.zh: sexuality 由 sexual 加名词后缀 -ity 构成；sexual 最终源于拉丁语 sexus，意为“性别”。这个词从与性有关的性质或状态，发展为对性欲、性表达和性取向的概括。
etymology_story.en: Sexuality was formed from sexual and the noun suffix -ity; sexual ultimately comes from Latin sexus, meaning 'sex'. Its meaning developed from a quality or condition relating to sex into a broader concept covering sexual desire, expression, and orientation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：sexual（性的）+ -ity（性质、状态）→ sexuality（性及相关属性）；sexual 本身可分析为 sex + -ual。主要词族：sex（性；性别）、sexual（性的）、sexually（在性方面）、sexuality（性；性取向）、sexualize/sexualise（使性化）、sexualization/sexualisation（性化）、nonsexual（非性的）；相关取向词包括 asexual/asexuality（无性恋的／无性恋）、bisexual/bisexuality（双性恋的／双性恋）、heterosexual/heterosexuality（异性恋的／异性恋）、homosexual/homosexuality（同性恋的／同性恋）及 pansexual/pansexuality（泛性恋的／泛性恋）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: sexual + -ity, a suffix expressing a quality or state, → sexuality; sexual itself can be analyzed as sex + -ual. Main family: sex, sexual, sexually, sexuality, sexualize/sexualise, sexualization/sexualisation, and nonsexual. Related orientation terms include asexual/asexuality, bisexual/bisexuality, heterosexual/heterosexuality, homosexual/homosexuality, and pansexual/pansexuality.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sexual orientation（性取向）专指性吸引的指向；sex drive（性欲）强调欲望的强弱；sensuality（感官享受；感官魅力）强调感官愉悦，并不一定涉及性。sexuality 的范围更广，可以涵盖欲望、表达和身份认同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sexual orientation specifically concerns patterns of sexual attraction; sex drive emphasizes the strength of sexual desire; sensuality concerns sensory pleasure or appeal and need not be sexual. Sexuality is broader and can encompass desire, expression, and identity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sexual（性的）+ -ity（整体性质）：把与性有关的感受、表达和取向合成一个概念。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sexual + -ity packages sexual feelings, expression, and orientation into one overall concept.

etymology_story.zh: simplify 经法语 simplifier 进入英语，可追溯到中世纪拉丁语 simplificare，其构词成分与拉丁语 simplex（简单的）和 facere（做；使成为）有关。“使简单”的基本含义延续至今，也用于数学上的化简。
etymology_story.en: Simplify entered English through French simplifier and goes back to Medieval Latin simplificare, formed from elements associated with Latin simplex, 'simple', and facere, 'make'. Its basic meaning of making something simple survives in both everyday use and mathematics.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：simple 去掉词尾不发音的 e，再加 -ify（使成为）→ simplify。主要词族：simple（简单的）、simply（简单地；仅仅）、simplicity（简单；质朴）、simplify（简化）、simplification（简化）、simplifier（简化者；简化工具）、simplified（简化的）、oversimplify（过度简化）、oversimplification（过度简化）、simplistic（过分简单化的）、simplistically（过分简单化地）。动词变化：simplifies、simplified、simplifying。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: simple loses its final silent e and takes -ify, meaning 'make or become', → simplify. Main family: simple, simply, simplicity, simplify, simplification, simplifier, simplified, oversimplify, oversimplification, simplistic, and simplistically. Verb forms: simplifies, simplified, and simplifying.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: clarify（澄清）侧重消除含混；streamline（精简）侧重删减流程中的多余环节以提高效率；reduce（减少；化简）强调数量、规模或形式的缩减。simplify 强调降低复杂程度，未必减少内容。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Clarify focuses on removing ambiguity; streamline removes unnecessary stages to improve efficiency; reduce emphasizes a decrease in amount, size, or form. Simplify focuses on lowering complexity and does not necessarily remove content.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: simple + -ify：把复杂的东西“变简单”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Simple + -ify: make something simple.

etymology_story.zh: sometime 源于中古英语中 some 与 time 的组合，早期也有“从前”的意思。现代副词主要表示某个未确定的时间，形容词则保留“曾经的”，也可表示“偶尔的”。
etymology_story.en: Sometime developed from a Middle English combination of some and time and also had the early meaning 'formerly'. The modern adverb mainly indicates an unspecified time, while the adjective retains 'former' and can also mean 'occasional'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：some（某个）+ time（时间）→ sometime，是复合词，没有常用的屈折变化或直接派生词。相关形式须区分：sometime 指某个时间；sometimes 指有时、偶尔；some time 是两个词，指一段时间。形容词 sometime 通常放在名词前，语体较正式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: some + time → sometime, a compound with no usual inflections or direct derivatives. Distinguish the related forms: sometime means at an unspecified time; sometimes means on some occasions; some time is a two-word phrase meaning a period of time. The adjective sometime normally precedes a noun and is relatively formal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: someday（有朝一日）只指未来，常带愿望色彩；former（从前的）对应形容词 sometime 的过去身份义；occasional（偶尔的）对应其间或参与义。副词 sometime 既可指未来，也可指过去。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Someday refers only to the future and often suggests a hope; former matches the adjective's past-role meaning; occasional matches its intermittent-role meaning. The adverb sometime can refer to either the future or the past.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: some + time＝某个时间点；sometimes＝有时；some time＝一段时间。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sometime: an unspecified point; sometimes: on some occasions; some time: a period.

etymology_story.zh: specialty 经古法语 specialte 等形式传入英语，最终源于拉丁语 specialitas（特殊性），与 specialis（特殊的）同源。“特殊之处”的含义后来发展为个人专长、专业分支和地方或商家的特色产品。
etymology_story.en: Specialty entered English through Old French forms such as specialte and ultimately derives from Latin specialitas, 'particularity', related to specialis, 'special'. The idea of a distinguishing quality developed into expertise, a professional branch, and a characteristic local or commercial product.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 special（特殊的）+ -ty（性质或状态）→ specialty；历史上它是借入词。主要词族：special（特殊的）、specially（专门地）、specialness（特殊性）、specialty/speciality（专长；特色产品）、specialist（专家；专科医生）、specialism（专业领域）、specialize/specialise（专攻）、specialized/specialised（专业化的）、specialization/specialisation（专业化）。specialty 主要用于美式英语，英式英语通常用 speciality；复数为 specialties。名词前的修饰用法也可分析为名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern analysis is special + -ty, a noun suffix expressing a quality or state, → specialty, although historically the word was borrowed. Main family: special, specially, specialness, specialty/speciality, specialist, specialism, specialize/specialise, specialized/specialised, and specialization/specialisation. Specialty is chiefly American; British English usually uses speciality. The plural is specialties. Its modifying use before a noun can also be analyzed as an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: expertise（专业知识与技能）强调能力本身；specialization（专门化；专业方向）强调聚焦某一领域的过程或结果；signature dish（招牌菜）专指体现餐馆或厨师特色的菜品。specialty 可以指人的专长、专业分支，也可以指特色产品。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Expertise emphasizes knowledge and skill themselves; specialization emphasizes the process or result of concentrating on a field; signature dish specifically identifies a dish associated with a restaurant or chef. Specialty can name a person's strength, a professional branch, or a distinctive product.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 special 想到“特别拿手、特别有名”：人有专长，店有招牌，地方有特产。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with special: a person's special skill, a shop's signature offering, or a place's distinctive product.

usage_note: systematic 强调按照计划、顺序或规则进行，而不是零散尝试。

senses.meaning_zh: 系统的；有条理的；按计划或固定方法进行的
senses.meaning_en: organized and carried out according to a plan or consistent method
senses.english_definition: Something that is systematic is done in an organized way, following a plan or a consistent method.
senses.collocation_en: a systematic approach; a systematic review
senses.collocation_zh: 系统的方法；系统性综述
senses.sentence_en: We need a systematic approach to identifying and fixing these errors.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们需要采用系统的方法来识别并修正这些错误。

etymology_story.zh: systematic 最终源于希腊语 systēmatikos，意为“组合成整体的”，与 systēma（组合而成的整体）有关，并经后来的拉丁语和法语形式传播。“各部分组成整体”的观念在现代英语中发展为“按照一致的方法和步骤组织起来”。
etymology_story.en: Systematic ultimately comes from Greek systēmatikos, 'combined into a whole', related to systēma, 'an organized whole', and was transmitted through later Latin and French forms. The idea of parts forming a whole developed into the modern meaning of being organized according to consistent methods and steps.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：system（系统）+ -atic（构成相关形容词）→ systematic。主要词族：system（系统）、systematic（系统的）、systematically（系统地）、unsystematic（无系统的）、unsystematically（无系统地）、systematize/systematise（使系统化）、systematization/systematisation（系统化）、systematizer/systematiser（使事物系统化的人或工具）。相关词 systemic（全系统的；影响整体的）及 systemically（在全系统层面）意义不同，不能直接当作 systematic 及 systematically 的替代词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: system + the adjective-forming suffix -atic → systematic. Main family: system, systematic, systematically, unsystematic, unsystematically, systematize/systematise, systematization/systematisation, and systematizer/systematiser. Related systemic and systemically refer to a whole system or effects throughout it and are not direct substitutes for systematic and systematically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: methodical（有条不紊的）强调按步骤细致推进；organized（有组织的；有条理的）强调安排妥当；structured（有明确结构的）强调框架和顺序。systematic 尤其强调按照一致的方法，全面而有序地处理问题。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Methodical emphasizes careful progress through steps; organized emphasizes effective arrangement; structured emphasizes a clear framework and sequence. Systematic particularly suggests consistent methods applied in an orderly and comprehensive way.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: system 是系统，systematic 就是让行动也按系统运行：有步骤、有顺序、有方法。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A system has an order; systematic work follows that order through clear steps and consistent methods.

senses.meaning_en: very badly; in a very unpleasant or harmful way

etymology_story.zh: terribly 由 terrible 加副词后缀形成；terrible 经法语源自拉丁语 terribilis，原义为“令人恐惧的”。词义由“可怕地、糟糕地”扩展为表示强烈程度的“非常”，此时未必含有负面评价。
etymology_story.en: Terribly was formed from terrible with an adverb suffix; terrible came through French from Latin terribilis, meaning 'frightening'. Its meaning broadened from 'in a dreadful or bad way' to the intensifier 'very', which does not necessarily express a negative judgment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：terrible → 去掉词尾 -le，加 -ly → terribly。常见词族：terrible（可怕的；糟糕的）、terribly（非常；糟糕地）、terribleness（可怕；糟糕，较少用）；terror（恐惧）属于历史相关词，不能把 terribly 直接分析为 terror + -ly。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: terrible → replace final -le with -ly → terribly. The main derivative family includes terrible, terribly, and the less common noun terribleness; terror is historically related, but terribly is not formed directly as terror + -ly.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: very 是中性的程度词；extremely 更明确地表示程度极高；badly 对应“糟糕地、严重地”这一义项，不能替代 terribly 的所有程度用法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Very is a neutral intensifier; extremely more explicitly indicates a very high degree; badly matches the poor-performance or harmful-manner sense and cannot replace terribly in every intensifying use.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 terrible“糟糕的”出发：动作做得糟糕是 terribly，程度强到惊人也可以用 terribly。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with terrible: terribly can describe doing something badly or intensify something to a striking degree.

senses.english_definition: The thickness of something such as hair or vegetation is how densely its individual parts grow or are packed together.
senses.collocation_en: the thickness of her hair; the thickness of the vegetation
senses.collocation_zh: 她头发的浓密程度；植被的茂密程度

etymology_story.zh: thickness 源于古英语中由表示“厚的”的词加名词后缀构成的形式，与现代 thick 和 -ness 一脉相承。它既表示物体的厚度，也随 thick 的常用义项表示液体的浓稠程度和事物的浓密程度。
etymology_story.en: Thickness goes back to an Old English noun formed from the adjective meaning 'thick' and a noun-forming suffix, corresponding to modern thick and -ness. Alongside physical thickness, it expresses the consistency of liquids and the density of things, following the senses of thick.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：thick（厚的；浓的）+ -ness（性质、状态）→ thickness；可数义的复数为 thicknesses。常见词族：thick、thickly（厚厚地；密集地）、thickness、thicken（变厚；使变稠）、thickens、thickened、thickening（变厚；增稠；增厚处）、thickener（增稠剂）；另有 thickish（略厚的）及 thickset（粗壮的）、thick-skinned（厚脸皮的；不易受伤害的）等复合词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: thick + -ness, a suffix expressing a quality or state → thickness; the countable plural is thicknesses. The main family includes thick, thickly, thickness, thicken, thickens, thickened, thickening, and thickener; further forms include thickish and compounds such as thickset and thick-skinned.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: depth 可指从表面向内或向下的距离，与 thickness 在部分测量语境中重叠；density 强调单位空间内的密集程度，不等于厚度；viscosity 是表示流体抗流动能力的技术词，比日常所说的“浓稠度”更精确。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Depth measures distance inward or downward and overlaps with thickness in some measurements; density concerns how closely matter or items are packed, rather than thickness itself; viscosity is the technical measure of resistance to flow and is more precise than everyday thickness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: thick 是“厚、浓”，-ness 把性质变成名词：厚到什么程度，就是 thickness。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Thick names the quality; -ness turns it into a noun: thickness tells you how thick something is.

senses.meaning_zh: 在……下面；被……覆盖着
senses.meaning_en: directly under or covered by something
senses.english_definition: If something is underneath another thing, it is directly below it or covered by it.

senses.collocation_zh: 在床下面；被一层灰尘覆盖着
senses.sentence_en: She found her keys underneath a pile of papers.
senses.sentence_zh: 她在一摞文件下面找到了钥匙。

senses.meaning_zh: 在……表象之下；隐藏在……背后
senses.meaning_en: behind an outward appearance or beneath an apparent quality
senses.english_definition: If a feeling or quality exists underneath an outward appearance, it is present but hidden by that appearance.

senses.collocation_zh: 在表象之下；在他平静的外表之下
senses.sentence_en: Underneath his calm exterior, he was deeply worried.
senses.sentence_zh: 在平静的外表之下，他内心十分担忧。

senses.meaning_zh: 在下面；在底下；在下层
senses.meaning_en: in a position below something or on its lower side
senses.english_definition: If something is underneath, it is below something else or on the lower side of it.
senses.collocation_en: the apartment underneath; wear a shirt underneath

senses.meaning_zh: 内心里；实际上；在表象之下
senses.meaning_en: in someone's true character or feelings beneath their outward appearance
senses.english_definition: You use underneath to describe what someone is really like or really feels, although they may appear different.
senses.collocation_en: kind underneath; underneath it all
senses.collocation_zh: 内心善良；在所有表象之下
senses.sentence_en: She can seem unfriendly, but she's very kind underneath.
senses.sentence_zh: 她有时看起来不太友好，但内心很善良。

etymology_story.zh: underneath 源自古英语中由 under 与另一个表示“在下方”的成分组成的复合形式，原本就强调较低的位置。后来，空间上的“在下面”自然延伸为“隐藏在外表之下”。
etymology_story.en: Underneath comes from an Old English compound combining under with another element meaning 'below', originally emphasizing a lower position. Its spatial meaning later extended naturally to qualities or feelings hidden beneath an outward appearance.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 underneath 作为完整词使用，不把词尾机械地分析为可自由套用的后缀；可借 under + neath 理解其历史结构，但 neath 在现代主要见于诗歌形式 'neath。underneath 本身没有常用的屈折或派生形式；相关位置词包括 under（在……下面）和 beneath（在……下方），它们不是 underneath 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, underneath is normally treated as a whole word, without a productive suffix at its end; under + neath can illuminate its historical structure, but neath now survives chiefly in poetic 'neath. Underneath has no common inflected or derived forms; related positional words include under and beneath, which are not derivatives of underneath.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: under 用途最广，既表示空间位置，也表示控制或状态；beneath 较正式，也可表示“有失身份”；below 强调位置或数值较低，不一定在正下方。underneath 常突出正下方、遮盖关系或隐藏的内在。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Under has the broadest uses, including position, control, and conditions; beneath is more formal and can also mean unworthy of someone's status; below indicates a lower position or value without necessarily meaning directly under. Underneath often highlights direct position, covering, or a concealed inner reality.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先看 under“在下方”，再记 underneath 的画面：上面盖着，东西或真实内心藏在下面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use under as the starting point: picture something covering what lies underneath, whether an object or a hidden feeling.

etymology_story.zh: unemployed 由否定前缀 un- 加 employed 构成，表示“不处于受雇状态”。其基础词 employ 经法语追溯到意为“卷入、使参与”的拉丁语 implicare，后来发展出“使用”和“雇用”的意思。
etymology_story.en: Unemployed was formed by adding negative un- to employed, meaning 'not in employment'. The base employ came through French from Latin implicare, meaning 'enfold or involve', and developed the senses 'use' and 'hire'.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：un-（不）+ employed（受雇的）；employed = employ + -ed。常见词族：employ（雇用）、employs、employed、employing、employer（雇主）、employee（雇员）、employment（就业）、unemployed（失业的）、unemployment（失业）、employable（具备就业能力的）、employability（就业能力）、unemployable（不具备就业条件的）、reemploy／re-employ（重新雇用）、reemployment／re-employment（重新就业）、self-employed（自雇的）、self-employment（自雇）、underemployed（就业不足的）、underemployment（就业不足）。the unemployed 指一类人，通常接复数谓语；不能用 an unemployed 表示“一名失业者”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: un- 'not' + employed; employed = employ + -ed. The main family includes employ, employs, employed, employing, employer, employee, employment, unemployed, unemployment, employable, employability, unemployable, reemploy/re-employ, reemployment/re-employment, self-employed, self-employment, underemployed, and underemployment. The unemployed refers collectively to people and normally takes plural agreement; an unemployed is not the standard expression for one unemployed person.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: jobless 同样表示没有工作，常见于新闻报道；out of work 是常用短语，强调目前没有工作；redundant 在英式英语中通常指因岗位不再需要而被裁减，强调失去工作的原因。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Jobless also means without work and is common in news reporting; out of work is an everyday phrase emphasizing the current situation; redundant, especially in British English, usually describes someone whose job has been removed because it is no longer needed.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: employed 是“受雇的”，前面加 un- 就是“没有受雇的”；the unemployed 把这类人作为一个群体来指称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Employed means having a job; un- reverses that state. Add the to refer collectively to people in that situation.

translation: 她在国外生活几年后，口音发生了轻微变化。

senses.meaning_zh: 口音；腔调
senses.meaning_en: a way of pronouncing a language associated with a place or social group
senses.english_definition: An accent is a way of pronouncing a language that shows which country, region, or social group someone comes from.
senses.collocation_en: a strong accent; speak with an accent

senses.sentence_en: She speaks English with a slight French accent.

senses.meaning_zh: 重音；重读
senses.meaning_en: extra prominence given to a syllable, word, or musical note
senses.english_definition: An accent is extra emphasis given to a particular syllable, word, or musical note.
senses.collocation_en: the accent on the first syllable; a strong musical accent
senses.collocation_zh: 第一音节上的重音；鲜明的音乐重音

senses.meaning_zh: 变音符号；重音符号
senses.meaning_en: a written mark indicating pronunciation, stress, or tone
senses.english_definition: An accent is a mark written above or below a letter to indicate something about its pronunciation, stress, or tone.
senses.collocation_en: an acute accent; a grave accent
senses.collocation_zh: 尖音符；重音符

senses.meaning_zh: 重点；着重之处
senses.meaning_en: special emphasis or importance given to something
senses.english_definition: If the accent is on something, particular importance or attention is given to it.
senses.collocation_en: put the accent on quality; the accent is on teamwork
senses.collocation_zh: 着重质量；重点是团队合作
senses.sentence_en: The course puts the accent on practical communication.
senses.sentence_zh: 这门课程着重培养实际交流能力。

senses.meaning_zh: 装饰亮点；点缀
senses.meaning_en: a contrasting detail that adds interest or emphasis
senses.english_definition: An accent is a detail, often a contrasting colour or object, that makes a design or appearance more interesting.
senses.collocation_en: colour accents; decorative accents
senses.collocation_zh: 色彩点缀；装饰性点缀

senses.meaning_zh: 突出；强调；使显眼

senses.english_definition: If something accents a feature, it makes that feature stand out or become more noticeable.
senses.collocation_en: accent a feature; accent the waist
senses.collocation_zh: 突出某个特点；突出腰线

senses.sentence_zh: 一条细腰带突出了腰线。

senses.meaning_zh: 重读；给……加重音

senses.english_definition: If you accent a syllable, word, or musical note, you give it extra emphasis when speaking or performing.
senses.collocation_en: accent the first syllable; accent the first beat

etymology_story.zh: accent 经法语源于拉丁语 accentus，意为“声调、语调”，与 ad-（向、加于）和 cantus（歌唱）有关。它从声音的调子和重音，发展出地区口音、书写符号，以及强调和装饰点缀等意义。
etymology_story.en: Accent came through French from Latin accentus, meaning 'tone or intonation', associated with ad- 'to' and cantus 'singing'. From vocal tone and stress, it developed senses referring to regional pronunciation, written marks, and emphasis or decorative highlights.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 accent 是完整词干，可作名词或动词，不宜把其历史成分当作现代可自由组合的词缀。常见词族：accent、accents、accented（带口音的；带重音或符号的）、accenting、unaccented（不重读的；无变音符号的）、accentual（重音的）、accentless（无明显口音的，较少用）、accentuate（突出；强调）、accentuated、accentuating、accentuation（强调；重音配置）。名词通常首音节重读；动词可末音节重读，也有首音节重读的读法。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, accent is a whole stem used as a noun or verb; its historical elements should not be treated as freely productive modern affixes. The main family includes accent, accents, accented, accenting, unaccented, accentual, the less common accentless, accentuate, accentuated, accentuating, and accentuation. The noun normally has initial stress; the verb can have final stress, with an initial-stress pronunciation also established.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pronunciation 指发音方式或某个词的读法，范围比地区口音更广；dialect 指方言，除发音外还可涉及词汇和语法；emphasis 对应 accent 的“强调、重点”义，不表示地区口音。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pronunciation refers broadly to how speech sounds or individual words are produced; dialect includes vocabulary and grammar as well as pronunciation; emphasis corresponds to the stress or importance senses of accent, rather than a regional way of speaking.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“声音或特征凸显出来”：说话方式凸显是口音，音节凸显是重音，设计细节凸显是点缀。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of something standing out: a distinctive speaking pattern is an accent, a prominent syllable carries an accent, and a striking design detail adds an accent.

usage_note: actively 强调有实际行动和主动参与，而不是仅仅在场或知道。

senses.meaning_zh: 积极地；主动地；以实际行动
senses.meaning_en: with deliberate effort or practical involvement
senses.english_definition: If you actively do something, you make a deliberate effort to do it or take a practical part in it.

senses.collocation_en: actively growing; actively dividing cells
senses.collocation_zh: 正在旺盛生长；正在活跃分裂的细胞

senses.sentence_zh: 这种治疗针对的是正在活跃分裂的细胞。

etymology_story.zh: actively 是英语在 active 后加 -ly 形成的副词；active 经法语来自拉丁语 activus，与 agere（做、行动）及其分词 actus 有关。它保留了“实际行动、处于活动状态”的核心含义。
etymology_story.en: Actively was formed in English by adding -ly to active, which came through French from Latin activus, related to agere, meaning 'to do or act,' and its participle actus. It preserves the central idea of taking action or being in an active state.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：active（积极的；活动中的）+ -ly（副词后缀）→ actively。主要词族：act（行动；行为）、action（行动）、active（积极的；活跃的）、activity（活动）、activate（激活）、activation（激活）、activist（积极行动者）、activism（行动主义）；否定形式包括 inactive（不活跃的）、inactively（不活跃地）、inactivity（不活跃）及 deactivate/deactivation（停用／停用过程）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: active + the adverb suffix -ly → actively. Principal family members include act, action, active, activity, activate, activation, activist, and activism; negative or reversing forms include inactive, inactively, inactivity, deactivate, and deactivation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: proactively（主动预先地）强调提前采取行动；energetically（精力充沛地）强调投入的体力或热情；deliberately（有意地）强调意图。actively 的重点是实际参与或付诸行动，并不必然表示提前行动或精力旺盛。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Proactively emphasizes acting in advance; energetically emphasizes effort or enthusiasm; deliberately emphasizes intention. Actively chiefly indicates practical involvement or action, without necessarily implying anticipation or great energy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 act“行动”联想：actively 就是“实际行动起来地”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to act: actively means putting action into what you do.

senses.english_definition: An apple is a round fruit with firm flesh and red, green, or yellow skin.

senses.meaning_en: a tree that produces apples

senses.collocation_en: a flowering apple; plant an apple tree
senses.collocation_zh: 一棵开花的苹果树；种一棵苹果树

etymology_story.zh: apple 来自古英语 æppel，属于古老的日耳曼语词族，与德语 Apfel 同源。早期这个词的使用范围比现代更广，有时也泛指其他果实；现代通常专指苹果。
etymology_story.en: Apple comes from Old English æppel and belongs to an old Germanic word family that also includes German Apfel. Earlier usage could extend to other fruits, while the modern word normally identifies the familiar apple.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：apple 是不可再作常用词根与词缀拆分的基本名词；复数为 apples。常见复合词包括 apple tree（苹果树）、apple juice（苹果汁）、apple pie（苹果派）、applesauce（苹果酱）、apple cider（苹果酒；部分北美语境指未过滤苹果汁）、apple core（苹果核）和 apple blossom（苹果花）；apple 在这些词组中通常是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: apple is a simple noun without a productive root-and-affix division; its plural is apples. Common compounds include apple tree, apple juice, apple pie, applesauce, apple cider, apple core, and apple blossom; apple normally functions as a noun modifier in these expressions.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: apple 没有能在普通语境中完全替换它的常用近义词。fruit（水果）是上位词；pome（梨果）是植物学类别，包含苹果和梨；crab apple（海棠果；野苹果）指通常较小且较酸的相关果实。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Apple has no ordinary synonym that fully replaces it. Fruit is a broader category; pome is the botanical fruit type that includes apples and pears; crab apple identifies a related fruit that is usually smaller and more sour.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 基本词直接连实物：一个圆苹果 → apple；无需硬拆词根。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link this basic word directly to the object: picture one round apple, without inventing a root breakdown.

usage_note: authority 可指有权作决定的人或机构，也可指某人在某领域拥有的专业权威。

senses.meaning_zh: 权力；职权；管辖权
senses.meaning_en: the recognized power or right to make decisions and give orders
senses.english_definition: If you have authority, you have the recognized power or right to make decisions, give orders, or control something.
senses.collocation_en: have authority over; exercise authority
senses.collocation_zh: 对……有管辖权；行使职权

senses.meaning_zh: 正式许可；授权
senses.meaning_en: official permission to do something
senses.english_definition: Authority to do something is official permission to do it.
senses.collocation_en: without authority; written authority
senses.collocation_zh: 未经授权；书面授权
senses.sentence_en: No one may release these records without written authority.
senses.sentence_zh: 未经书面授权，任何人都不得公开这些记录。

senses.meaning_zh: 管理机构；当局；主管部门
senses.meaning_en: an official organization responsible for a particular area or activity
senses.english_definition: An authority is an official organization that manages a particular area or activity; the authorities are the officials or organizations in charge.
senses.collocation_en: local authority; the relevant authorities
senses.collocation_zh: 地方管理机构；有关部门
senses.sentence_en: The local authority is responsible for maintaining the park.
senses.sentence_zh: 当地主管部门负责维护这座公园。

senses.meaning_zh: 权威专家；公认的可靠资料来源
senses.meaning_en: a recognized expert or a trusted source of information
senses.english_definition: An authority on a subject is a person or source that people trust because of its knowledge or expertise.
senses.collocation_en: a leading authority on; a recognized authority
senses.collocation_zh: ……方面的顶尖权威；公认的权威
senses.sentence_en: She is a leading authority on medieval Chinese history.
senses.sentence_zh: 她是中国中世纪史研究领域的顶尖权威。

senses.meaning_zh: 威信；令人信服的力量
senses.meaning_en: the confidence, credibility, or influence that makes others listen and believe
senses.english_definition: If someone speaks or acts with authority, they seem knowledgeable and confident, so other people take them seriously.
senses.collocation_en: speak with authority; moral authority
senses.collocation_zh: 说话有说服力；道德威信
senses.sentence_en: Her years of practical experience allow her to speak with authority.
senses.sentence_zh: 多年的实践经验使她说话很有说服力。

etymology_story.zh: authority 经古法语 autorité 来自拉丁语 auctoritas，原指创始者、担保者或有威望者所具有的影响力与认可；其相关词 auctor 也产生了英语 author。词义后来发展为公认的权力、正式授权、管理机构，以及知识上的权威。
etymology_story.en: Authority came through Old French autorité from Latin auctoritas, referring to the influence or standing of an originator, guarantor, or respected person; the related noun auctor also gave English author. Its meanings developed to include recognized power, official permission, governing bodies, and expertise.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析：authority 是借入后整体使用的名词，不宜简单解释为现代 author（作者）+ -ity。主要词族：authorities（复数；常指当局）、authoritative（权威的；可信的）、authoritatively（权威地）、authoritativeness（权威性）、authorize/authorise（授权）、authorization/authorisation（授权）、authorized/authorised（获授权的）、unauthorized/unauthorised（未经授权的）、authoritarian（专制的；专制主义者）、authoritarianism（专制主义）。author 与 authority 有历史同源关系。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: authority is a borrowed noun used as a whole, rather than a transparent formation from modern author plus -ity. Principal family members include authorities, authoritative, authoritatively, authoritativeness, authorize/authorise, authorization/authorisation, authorized/authorised, unauthorized/unauthorised, authoritarian, and authoritarianism. Author is historically related.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: power（权力；能力）范围更广，不一定得到认可；jurisdiction（管辖权）强调权力适用的地域或事务范围；expert（专家）强调专业知识，而 authority 还强调他人对其判断的公认与信赖。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Power is broader and need not be recognized as legitimate; jurisdiction specifies the area or matters over which power applies; expert emphasizes specialist knowledge, while authority also suggests recognized standing and trust.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“公认有资格”：有资格下令是职权，有资格作判断是权威，负责行使职权的是当局。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the senses in recognized standing: the standing to give orders is authority, the standing to judge makes an authority, and bodies exercising that power are authorities.

translation: 发送邀请前请查看会议室是否可用。
usage_note: availability 可表示物品是否有货、服务是否可用，或某人的时间是否空闲。

senses.meaning_zh: 可获得性；供应情况；可用性
senses.meaning_en: the state of being obtainable, accessible, or ready for use
senses.english_definition: The availability of something is whether or how easily people can obtain, access, or use it.
senses.collocation_en: subject to availability; limited availability
senses.collocation_zh: 视供应或空缺情况而定；供应有限
senses.sentence_en: Prices depend on the availability of rooms.
senses.sentence_zh: 价格取决于客房的空余情况。

senses.meaning_zh: 有空的情况；可参加或工作的时间
senses.meaning_en: the times when someone is free to meet, work, or take part
senses.english_definition: Your availability is the time when you are free to meet someone, work, or take part in an activity.
senses.collocation_en: confirm your availability; check someone's availability
senses.collocation_zh: 确认你有空的时间；查看某人何时有空
senses.sentence_en: Please let me know your availability for an interview next week.
senses.sentence_zh: 请告诉我你下周哪些时间可以参加面试。

senses.meaning_zh: 系统或服务的可用性；正常运行程度
senses.meaning_en: the extent to which a system or service is working and accessible
senses.english_definition: The availability of a system or service is how consistently it is working and can be used when needed.
senses.collocation_en: high availability; service availability
senses.collocation_zh: 高可用性；服务可用性
senses.sentence_en: The team monitors service availability around the clock.
senses.sentence_zh: 团队全天候监测服务的可用性。

etymology_story.zh: availability 由 available 加名词后缀 -ity 形成；available 原先与“有效用、能起作用”有关，后来发展为“可得到、可使用”。更深一层的 avail 经法语与拉丁语 valere（强健；有力量；有价值）有关。
etymology_story.en: Availability was formed from available with the noun suffix -ity; available developed from the idea of being useful or effective to being obtainable or usable. Further back, avail is connected through French with Latin valere, meaning 'to be strong, effective, or of worth.'

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：avail + -able → available；available + -ity → availability，其中 -able 对应变为 -ability。主要词族：avail（有帮助；利用）、available（可获得的；有空的）、availability（可获得性；空闲情况）、unavailable（不可获得的；没空的）、unavailability（无法获得；无空闲时间）；技术复合形式有 high-availability（高可用性的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: avail + -able → available; available + -ity → availability, with -able taking the corresponding -ability form. Principal family members are avail, available, availability, unavailable, and unavailability; a common technical compound modifier is high-availability.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: accessibility（可访问性；易获取程度）强调获取或使用是否方便、是否存在障碍；supply（供应量）强调现有或提供的数量；readiness（准备就绪）强调是否已经准备好。availability 主要回答“是否能获得、使用或安排”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Accessibility emphasizes ease of access and the absence of barriers; supply emphasizes the quantity provided or on hand; readiness emphasizes being prepared. Availability chiefly concerns whether something can be obtained, used, or scheduled.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: available 是“可用的”，availability 就是问“有没有得用、有没有空”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Available means ready or obtainable; availability asks, 'Can I get it, use it, or book the time?'

usage_note: bang 作名词表示突然、响亮的撞击或爆裂声，常与 hear、make 或 loud 搭配。

senses.meaning_zh: 突然的巨响；砰的一声
senses.meaning_en: a sudden loud noise, especially from an impact or explosion
senses.english_definition: A bang is a sudden loud noise, such as the sound of an explosion or a door closing hard.
senses.collocation_en: a loud bang; with a bang
senses.collocation_zh: 一声巨响；砰的一声
senses.sentence_en: We heard a loud bang outside the window.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们听见窗外传来一声巨响。

senses.meaning_zh: 猛撞；重击
senses.meaning_en: a hard knock or blow
senses.english_definition: A bang is a hard knock or blow against someone or something.
senses.collocation_en: a bang on the head; give something a bang
senses.collocation_zh: 头部受到的一下撞击；猛敲某物一下
senses.sentence_en: He got a nasty bang on the head when he fell.

senses.meaning_zh: 刘海；额前短发（美式英语，通常用复数 bangs）
senses.meaning_en: hair cut short so that it hangs over the forehead, usually called bangs in American English
senses.english_definition: Bangs are short pieces of hair that hang over your forehead; in British English, this hairstyle is usually called a fringe.
senses.collocation_en: cut bangs; straight bangs
senses.collocation_zh: 剪刘海；齐刘海
senses.sentence_en: She had her bangs trimmed before the wedding.
senses.sentence_zh: 婚礼前，她修剪了刘海。

senses.meaning_zh: 强烈的兴奋或乐趣（非正式，常见于固定表达）
senses.meaning_en: a strong feeling of excitement or enjoyment, used informally in set expressions
senses.english_definition: If you get a bang out of something, you get a lot of excitement or enjoyment from it.
senses.collocation_en: get a bang out of; a big bang for your buck
senses.collocation_zh: 从……中获得极大乐趣；花钱获得很大价值
senses.sentence_en: I still get a bang out of watching old comedy films.
senses.sentence_zh: 看老喜剧电影仍然让我乐在其中。

senses.meaning_en: an act of sexual intercourse, expressed vulgarly

senses.collocation_en: a quick bang; have a bang

senses.sentence_en: He crudely described the encounter as a quick bang.
senses.sentence_zh: 他粗俗地把那次接触形容为一次匆忙的性交。

senses.meaning_zh: 砰砰作响；猛敲
senses.meaning_en: to make a loud impact noise or hit something noisily
senses.english_definition: If something bangs, it makes a sudden loud noise; if you bang on something, you hit it to make a loud noise.
senses.collocation_en: bang on the door; a door banging shut
senses.collocation_zh: 砰砰敲门；砰的一声关上的门
senses.sentence_en: Someone was banging on the front door.
senses.sentence_zh: 有人正在砰砰地敲前门。

senses.meaning_zh: 撞到；使身体某部位重重碰上
senses.meaning_en: to hit something accidentally and forcefully
senses.english_definition: If you bang part of your body against something, you hit it hard, usually by accident.
senses.collocation_en: bang your head; bang into a table
senses.collocation_zh: 撞到头；撞上桌子
senses.sentence_en: I banged my knee against the edge of the desk.
senses.sentence_zh: 我的膝盖重重地撞到了书桌边缘。

senses.meaning_zh: 砰地关上；用力放下或扔下
senses.meaning_en: to close, put down, or move something forcefully and noisily
senses.english_definition: If you bang something shut or bang it down, you move it with enough force to make a loud noise.
senses.collocation_en: bang the door shut; bang a fist on the table
senses.collocation_zh: 砰地关上门；用拳头猛砸桌子
senses.sentence_en: She banged the door shut and walked away.
senses.sentence_zh: 她砰地关上门，走开了。

senses.meaning_en: exactly or precisely, used informally for emphasis
senses.english_definition: Bang means exactly, especially when you emphasize a place or time.
senses.collocation_en: bang in the middle; bang on time
senses.collocation_zh: 正好在中间；非常准时

senses.meaning_zh: 径直地；猛然地（非正式）
senses.meaning_en: directly, suddenly, or forcefully, used informally for emphasis

senses.sentence_en: He turned around and walked bang into a glass door.
